title: Isandro and the Verdict Again
premise: Bram Hartwell is hired by a dying woman, Odile Vane, to prove that her brother Isandro—who vanished thirty years ago—has not yet been murdered, a crime she insists is foretold in letters she's begun receiving. As Bram traces the estate, he discovers Isandro never left: his identity was stolen the night of a fire, and someone in the close-knit household that 'found' him has been living his life ever since. The alibis from thirty years ago were built to protect a child who witnessed everything, and now that child—grown, powerful, and cornered—is preparing to make the prophecy true. Bram must choose between loyalty to his client's found family and the truth, exposing the killer in the very house where Isandro has been hidden in plain sight all along.
about_author: E. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade watching families unravel over paper. They write mysteries about documents that lie and the people who sign them.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Bram Hartwell, POV. A sealed envelope arrives containing a will dated next year, naming Bram as executor for a man not yet dead. His pride in closing every case wars with unease; he accepts anyway, telling himself it's a prank. Emotional beat: professional vanity masking dread.

chapters.title: Client in Advance
chapters.summary: Odile Vane, frail and lucid, pays triple to prove her brother Isandro hasn't been murdered—yet—and shows Bram the first of seven letters predicting it. Bram, POV. He takes the retainer against his better judgment. Beat: fascination overriding instinct.

chapters.title: Vane House
chapters.summary: Bram visits the crumbling Vane estate and meets the household that took Isandro in decades ago: matriarch Corliss, groundskeeper Pell, and Odile's nurse, Sable. Everyone is warm; everyone watches him too closely. Bram, POV. Beat: charm with teeth.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Paperwork
chapters.summary: In the county archives Bram finds the fire report from the night Isandro disappeared—body never recovered, death certificate signed by Corliss herself. Bram, POV. The legal impossibility hooks him fully. Beat: the thrill of a real puzzle.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: A second letter arrives at Odile's bedside before Bram can warn her, dated three days ahead and describing his own visit in detail. Bram, POV. He realizes the writer is watching the investigation itself. Beat: hunter becomes hunted.

chapters.title: Alibi, Woven
chapters.summary: Bram interviews each household member about the night of the fire; their stories interlock too perfectly, like a rehearsed play. Sable's account contradicts a weather record by one hour. Bram, POV. Beat: the first loose thread.

chapters.title: Isandro's Room
chapters.summary: Odile lets Bram into the sealed bedroom, untouched for thirty years: clothes, a half-written letter, and a child's drawing of five figures—one face scratched out. Bram, POV. Beat: grief preserved like a specimen.

chapters.title: The Half-Written Letter
chapters.summary: The letter is addressed to Odile and breaks off mid-sentence: 'If anything happens to me, it will be one of the people who—' Bram photographs everything. Someone has already searched the room; the dust tells him so. Bram, POV. Beat: violation within sanctuary.

chapters.title: Pell's Silence
chapters.summary: The groundskeeper catches Bram snooping in the boathouse and nearly throws him out, then quietly says: 'Ask about the winter Isandro came.' Bram, POV. Beat: an ally who cannot afford to be one.

chapters.title: Found Family Files
chapters.summary: Bram pulls adoption and guardianship records: Corliss legally became Isandro's guardian six weeks after the fire—before he was declared missing. The timeline is impossible. Bram, POV. Beat: the case turns from mystery to cover-up.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Vanes
chapters.summary: Corliss hosts an elegant dinner, probing Bram's past and offering to double whatever Odile paid. He declines; her smile doesn't waver. Bram, POV. Beat: temptation dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: Letter three predicts a break-in at the estate office—which happens that night, targeting the guardianship file. Bram arrives too late but finds a dropped cufflink engraved with initials that don't belong to anyone in the house. Bram, POV. Beat: escalation, physical stakes.

chapters.title: Sable's Story
chapters.summary: The nurse finally talks: she was a child in the house when Isandro arrived, and she remembers two boys, not one. She begs Bram to stop before 'the date' comes. Bram, POV. Beat: witness testimony wrapped in terror.

chapters.title: Two Boys
chapters.summary: Bram reconstructs school and medical records: Isandro had a twin, declared stillborn—or erased. One twin lived publicly; the other lived secretly. Which one vanished? Bram, POV. Beat: the premise inverts.

chapters.title: Odile Fails
chapters.summary: Odile suffers a stroke-like episode on the exact date letter four predicted—nonfatal, but proof the letters aren't bluffing. Bram realizes the prophecies are schedules, not predictions. Bram, POV. Beat: cold horror replaces curiosity.

chapters.title: The Archive Thief
chapters.summary: Bram stakes out the county records room and catches a courier destroying the original fire file—but the courier escapes, leaving behind a payment slip from the Vane trust. Bram, POV. Beat: the conspiracy has institutional reach.

chapters.title: Corliss, Cornered Gently
chapters.summary: Bram confronts Corliss with the guardianship timeline. She admits the paperwork was falsified—to protect a traumatized child, she claims—and warns him some mercies are worth their lies. Bram, POV. Beat: sympathy for the suspect.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Odile, recovering, asks Bram directly: if the truth destroys the only family she has left, does he still owe it to her? He can't answer. Bram, POV. Beat: thematic crux stated aloud.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Floor
chapters.summary: Pell finally opens the boathouse: beneath rotted planks, a hidden room with a cot, books, and thirty years of grocery receipts. Someone has been living there until very recently. Bram, POV. Beat: Isandro was never gone.

chapters.title: Recent Footprints
chapters.summary: The receipts end eleven months ago—the same month the letters began. Whoever lived in hiding either left or died, and the letters are written in their voice. Bram, POV. Beat: hope curdling into worse questions.

chapters.title: Handwriting
chapters.summary: A graphologist confirms the letters match Isandro's known hand—but samples show the signature changed subtly after the fire. Two writers, one name. Bram, POV. Beat: forensic confirmation of the twin theory.

chapters.title: The Fifth Letter
chapters.summary: Letter five names Bram himself: 'The lawyer will be given a choice.' That night his office is ransacked and his copy of the will stolen. Bram, POV. Beat: personal danger, no more observer status.

chapters.title: What the Will Says
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the will from memory, Bram decodes its odd clause: the estate passes entirely to 'Isandro Vane, living or otherwise'—a legal instrument designed to keep one specific person hidden or exposed. Bram, POV. Beat: the document was a trap all along.

chapters.title: Sable Disappears
chapters.summary: The nurse vanishes, leaving a note: 'I told you the date. It's sooner now.' Bram searches her quarters and finds childhood photos of the twins together—smiling. Bram, POV. Beat: guilt over pushing a witness too hard.

chapters.title: Pell Confesses Partly
chapters.summary: Pell admits he helped hide one twin after the fire because the other tried to smother him in his sleep; the family chose which boy to save. He won't say which. Bram, POV. Beat: the found family's founding sin revealed.

chapters.title: The Fire, Rebuilt
chapters.summary: Bram reconstructs the full night: the twins swapped identities during the chaos, one taking the dead boy's place in the world, the other taking the attic. The murder being prophesied is the second attempt. Bram, POV. Beat: the mechanism understood, the culprit still masked.

chapters.title: Corliss's Deathbed Version
chapters.summary: Corliss falls ill and gives Bram a confession designed to close the case neatly—naming herself as everything's author. Too neat. Bram, POV. Beat: a sacrifice play he refuses to accept.

chapters.title: Following the Money
chapters.summary: Trust disbursements reveal monthly payments to a private clinic under an alias—where, Bram discovers, a patient matching Isandro's description died last spring. Or was reported to. Bram, POV. Beat: the trail narrows to one building.

chapters.title: The Clinic
chapters.summary: Bram infiltrates the clinic and finds the patient file altered, but a nurse remembers a visitor: Sable, weekly, for years. The missing witness was tending the hidden twin. Bram, POV. Beat: allies reassessed.

chapters.title: Sable Found
chapters.summary: Bram tracks Sable to a coastal cottage where she's been protecting the surviving hidden twin—a broken man who believes he IS Isandro and that his brother stole his life twice. Bram, POV. Beat: pity and fear entwined.

chapters.title: Which Brother
chapters.summary: The hidden man's memories contradict the historical record; Bram realizes the household may have chosen wrong thirty years ago and built the alibis to bury the mistake. Bram, POV. Beat: truth becomes unfixed.

chapters.title: The Sixth Letter
chapters.summary: Letter six arrives, postmarked today, announcing the murder for tomorrow night at the estate—and asking Odile to forgive them. Bram races back through a storm. Bram, POV. Beat: countdown begins.

chapters.title: Gathering at Vane House
chapters.summary: All players converge: Corliss propped up in her chair, Pell armed, the returned Sable silent, and Odile insisting on witnessing whatever comes. Bram locks the doors himself. Bram, POV. Beat: the stage set.

chapters.title: The Verdict Again
chapters.summary: Bram stages a mock reading of the impossible will, forcing the household to relive the night of the fire aloud. Under pressure, the rehearsed alibis crack in sequence, each person revealing one true sentence. Bram, POV. Beat: climax begins—truth as pressure.

chapters.title: The Smothered Boy
chapters.summary: The confession detonates: the twin raised as Isandro attempted the murder as a child; the family hid the victim instead of the culprit, and the letters are the victim's long revenge—dictated through Sable, who loved him. Bram, POV. Beat: reversal—sympathy shifts.

chapters.title: Tomorrow Night
chapters.summary: The seventh letter's author stands revealed among them, and the final murder attempt begins in the locked house—Sable intervening, Pell wounded shielding Odile. Bram physically ends it. Bram, POV. Beat: action climax.

chapters.title: After the Reading
chapters.summary: Police take statements; the survivor-twin, both perpetrator and victim across thirty years, faces judgment while the found family shatters around the cost of its mercy. Bram testifies to all of it. Bram, POV. Beat: consequences without comfort.

chapters.title: Odile's Signature
chapters.summary: Dying, Odile signs a new, honest will—leaving the estate to a fund for children erased by their guardians—and thanks Bram for choosing truth over the family she loved. Bram, POV. Beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: Bram files the final papers, keeps the scratched-out child's drawing, and writes the case into his ledger as closed—not solved cleanly, but closed. He understands now why the client paid in advance. Bram, POV. Beat: melancholy resolution.

chapters.title: An Envelope, Unsealed
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Bram receives an eighth letter—blank except for a single line: 'Thank you for the verdict.' He burns it, or almost does. Bram, POV. Final beat: peace with a hairline crack, the loyal heart still listening.
